A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same soft-masked diffusion language modeling work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original continued-pretraining, coding, mathematical reasoning, and ablation results, including Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds training-from-scratch results, matched-compute evaluations, and diagnostic analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The default top-k feedback, confidence weighting, and training Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds an experimental full-vocabulary variant that propagates gradients through both forward passes, extending the training procedure within an ablation. New Algorithm 2 documents the existing inference approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebText, the same instruction-tuning corpora, HumanEval/MBPP and their plus versions, GSM8k, and Math-500. Training from scratch, different compute budgets, and additional generation diagnostics retain the existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds quantitative comparisons with AR, SEDD, GIDD+, and LDDM-M in Tables 1 and 4, and CADD/CANDI in Table 13 and Figure 9. These substantially expand the comparator set beyond v1's binary-masking comparisons. Several comparator results are imported; Figure 9 explicitly uses visually extracted published results.

E3.justification: v2 adds training from scratch and controls matching forward-pass budgets: 0.5M versus 1M scratch updates, 50k versus 100k continuation updates, and 16.75k versus 33.5k finetuning updates. It adds generative perplexity and entropy evaluation. The reported unconstrained-generation protocol changes from 5,008 samples at batch size 16 to 5,000 at batch size 1.

E4.justification: Beyond retained top-k and time-dependent masking studies, v2 tests full-vocabulary feedback and gradient propagation in language modeling, analyzes entropy-related generation failures, profiles inference overhead and caching, and examines an eight-token decoding trajectory (Appendices C.2–C.5). These address additional questions about design choices, computational cost, and decoding behavior.

E5.justification: Matched continuation, coding, and math experiments retain five-seed reporting with means and standard deviations; the coding top-k study retains its shared-seed setup. Additional result rows do not introduce a new statistical procedure or establish increased repetition. Repeat counts are not disclosed for the new scratch results.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial scratch, matched-compute, diagnostic, and comparator results. Existing scores also change: Dream-7B MBPP+ at NFE 1/2 changes from 65.0 to 54.7 for SM and 53.7 to 39.6 for the finetuned baseline, changing the reported gain from 11.3 to 15.1 points (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). Their cause is unexplained. MAUVE values change under revised sampling settings, so they do not establish same-setting improvements. Math results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the mathematical assertion that feedback makes the marginal distribution analytically intractable and interprets proxy-state training through the existing variational objective. This extends the theoretical rationale without deriving a new bound or proof. The original diffusion equations and interpolation argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and second introductory contribution expand from demonstrated continued-pretraining gains to superior performance from training SM from scratch. This broadens the claimed successful training regime, while retaining the central SM contribution and the coding and efficiency-integration claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of ReMDM's diversity-related MAUVE decline, the computational tradeoffs of full-vocabulary feedback, and inference overhead from top-k computation and reduced cache hits. Appendix D also qualifies comparisons across different backbones and evaluation systems. These substantially expand the mechanisms and applicability caveats, although the concluding limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds inference pseudocode, a code-repository link, and a statement that supplementary materials contain code and environments. It documents scratch-training resources, GPT-2-large generative-perplexity evaluation, profiling tools, and previously unspecified Fast-dLLM block lengths and throughput calculation. The PDFs support these disclosures, not independent verification of the linked resources.

R1.justification: New Appendix D positions SM against CADD, CANDI, Loopholing, CCDD, latent discrete diffusion models, and dInfer, distinguishing feedback representations, weighting, training costs, and adaptation capabilities. Section 5 also strengthens the connection to self-conditioning. This is substantial research positioning beyond the numerous publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The main section order and much original prose remain intact. Local rewrites revise the abstract, training explanation, experimental narrative, and related work; the appendices gain dedicated inference and concurrent-work sections. This extends the existing organization rather than extensively rewriting or reorganizing it.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial displays for scratch training, matched-compute results, additional metrics, and concurrent comparisons. New Figures 6, 7, and 9 show runtime components, a decoding trajectory, and comparator tradeoffs; Figure 5 gains ablation curves. Existing tables gain budget information or revised headers, while retained figures and tables are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v1's principal training comparisons matched updates despite SM's additional forward pass. v2 materially strengthens the evidence with forward-pass-matched controls across language modeling and coding, plus training-from-scratch evaluations (Tables 1, 2, and 9). Added diagnostics and reproducibility information clarify costs and implementation. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses, including unexplained MBPP+ revisions and small discrepancies between the runtime totals in Appendix C.4 and Figure 6.
